prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a parking lot collision claim. Injury: back strain. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1201; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a low-speed collision in a parking lot. Insured reports the other vehicle backed into the driver's side door while the insured was stopped. Police not called; both parties exchanged information at the scene. Photos of damage received from insured. Claimant's vehicle identified as the other party's. Liability appears likely to fall on the backing vehicle, pending statements.

Entry 2: Contact made with the claimant's attorney's office. Counsel confirmed representation and requested that all communication go through their office. Claimant reports a back strain from the impact and has been seeking outpatient treatment. Requested medical records and treatment itemization. Counsel indicated a demand package will follow once treatment concludes.

Entry 3: Vehicle inspection completed at the repair facility. Rear quarter panel and driver's door show deformation consistent with the reported impact. Repair estimate received and under review. Noted no airbag deployment and no evidence of frame damage. Recorded inspection photos to file.

Entry 4: Received treatment records from the claimant's provider. Diagnosis is lumbar strain with muscle spasm. Treatment plan includes physical therapy sessions and periodic follow-up visits. Records indicate no prior back complaints in the past five years, though this is still being verified against prior claim history. Forwarded records to the medical review desk for evaluation.

Entry 5: Followed up with counsel regarding outstanding itemized bills and an updated treatment status. Counsel reports claimant is still attending physical therapy and expects to reach maximum medical improvement in the coming weeks. Reserves reviewed and adjusted to reflect the ongoing injury claim. Will continue monitoring and schedule a status review once the demand is received.
